items.title: Steve Turré interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 29, 2021
items.q: Rahsaan I first played with when I was 18 in San Francisco... once I came to New York I played with him again up until he passed.

ctx.x: Okay. Was there a particular artist, you mentioned John Coltrane a little bit ago, and I wonder if there was a particular artist that you started listening to that was an on-spot example of what you’re talking about with the spirit, not just the technique and the instrumental prowess, but the spirit behind it?

I’ll give you a good example. My first big boss that took me around the world, Ray Charles, he had nothing but soul, nothing but soul there. No matter what he plays. He plays all kinds of music. A direct connection. Rahsaan Roland Kirk is another one. Rahsaan I first played with when I was 18 in San Francisco, before I left the Bay area, when he was in town I would play with him.
I’m wondering what was going through your head on the way home after that performance with Rahsaan Roland Kirk?

items.title: Steve Turré interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 29, 2021
items.q: Steve Turré is an influential trombonist and has distinguished himself with Roland Kirk, Dizzy Gillespie, and as a leader with his own ensembles.

ctx.x: Steve Turré is an influential trombonist and has distinguished himself with Roland Kirk, Dizzy Gillespie, and as a leader with his own ensembles. He is an innovator with the use of conch shells in contemporary music.
Steve was interviewed via Zoom on November 29, 2021 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
